import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 60

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/60](https://www.erdosproblems.com/60)
- [HeMaYa21] He, J. and Ma, J. and Yang, T., *Some extremal results on 4-cycles*. Journal of
  Combinatorial Theory B (2021).
-/

namespace Erdos60

open SimpleGraph Filter
open scoped Real

/--
Does every graph on $n$ vertices with $>\mathrm{ex}(n;C_4)$ edges contain $\gg n^{1/2}$ many
copies of $C_4$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_60 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
          (c * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/- ## Variants and partial results -/

/--
He, Ma, and Yang [HeMaYa21] proved the conjecture when $n = q^2 + q + 1$ for some even integer $q$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧
      ∀ (q : ℕ) (_hq : Even q),
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (q^2 + q + 1))) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          (extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
          (c * Real.sqrt ((q^2 + q + 1) : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Simonovits conjectured that at least 2 copies of $C_4$ are guaranteed.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_60.variants.two_copies :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
        (2 ≤ { H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard) := by
  sorry

end Erdos60

findings.description: The theorem requires the supersaturation bound above `extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4)` for every even natural q. The cited He–Ma–Yang theorem instead uses the explicit threshold M(q) = q(q+1)^2/2; its corollary using the actual extremal number is for q = 2^k. These thresholds are not equal for arbitrary even q. The paper explicitly notes that ex(q^2+q+1,C4) ≤ M(q) − 0.2q for infinitely many even orders without a projective plane. For such large q, adding an edge to an extremal C4-free graph gives a graph satisfying the Lean hypothesis but below the paper's threshold. Thus Lean asserts an additional family of cases, not merely an equivalent reformulation of the cited result. The webpage's broad 'even integer' summary explains the discrepancy, but disagrees with the primary paper.
findings.source_evidence: He, Ma and Yang, Some extremal results on 4-cycles, Theorem 1.3 (author PDF p. 2), assumes even q ≥ 10^12 and exactly q(q+1)^2/2 + 1 edges. Immediately afterwards the authors state the extremal-number corollary specifically: 'For q = 2^k where k ≥ 40, any graph with q^2+q+1 vertices and ex(q^2+q+1,C4)+1 edges contains at least q−1 many C4's.' The remark after Theorem 1.2 (p. 1) establishes the strict threshold gap for infinitely many even q. Source: http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/c4-turan.pdf. These statements are also reproduced in arXiv:1912.00986v4, Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.7. In contrast, https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/60 summarizes the result using 'some even integer q'.
findings.suggested_fix: To retain the extremal-number hypothesis, restrict q to even prime powers, for example by adding `∃ k : ℕ, q = 2 ^ (k + 1)` or reparametrizing by k. Keeping all such k is harmless after reducing the unspecified positive constant. Alternatively, retain arbitrary even q but use the explicit threshold q(q+1)^2/2 and state the result for sufficiently large q, as in Theorem 1.3. Update the docstring to distinguish these two formulations.

status_issues.source_status: The cited source presents the general large-n two-copy bound as an unproved weaker Erdős–Simonovits conjecture, not as a solved partial result.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/60 says Erdős and Simonovits 'could not even prove that at least 2 copies of C4 are guaranteed'; it records only the special-order He–Ma–Yang progress. The introduction of arXiv:1912.00986v4 likewise identifies h(n) ≥ 2 for large n as the weak version of the conjecture. Neither source records a solution of this general statement.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research open`, unless an accepted proof of the general large-n two-copy statement can be supplied. The mathematical statement itself need not change.

reformulations.difference: The original literature formulates the bound using h(n), the minimum number of C4 copies among graphs with exactly ex(n,C4)+1 edges. Lean quantifies over all graphs with strictly more than ex(n,C4) edges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: From any graph with more than ex(n,C4) edges, delete surplus edges to leave exactly ex(n,C4)+1. Every C4 subgraph of the resulting graph remains a C4 subgraph of the original, so the same lower bound, constant, and eventual cutoff apply. The converse follows immediately because ex(n,C4)+1 > ex(n,C4). Proved in scratch as `Review60.main_iff_exact_threshold`, using an injective inclusion of the counted subgraphs.

reformulations.difference: The literature's weaker conjecture is h(n) ≥ 2 for large n, using graphs with exactly one edge beyond the extremal number; Lean covers every graph above the extremal number.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting surplus edges reduces to the exact-one-extra-edge case without increasing the number of C4 copies. Conversely, the exact-one-extra-edge case is included in the strict-inequality formulation. The full eventual equivalence was proved as `Review60.two_copies_iff_exact_threshold`.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/60 and https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/60 (read through their r.jina.ai text mirrors because direct requests returned Cloudflare challenges).

He, J.; Ma, J.; Yang, T., Some extremal results on 4-cycles, Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 149 (2021), 92–108, DOI 10.1016/j.jctb.2021.01.007. Author manuscript: http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/c4-turan.pdf, especially pp. 1–3.

He, J.; Ma, J.; Yang, T., Some exact results on 4-cycles: stability and supersaturation, arXiv:1912.00986v4: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.00986 and LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/1912.00986. Read the introduction, Section 7 on extremal thresholds, and concluding remarks.
http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/ — publication list locating the cited paper and distinguishing it from the follow-up.

Local Mathlib sources: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/{Extremal/Basic,CycleGraph,Subgraph,Copy,Maps,Finite,Basic}.lean; Data/Set/Card.lean; Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean; Order/Filter/AtTopBot/{Defs,Basic}.lean.

Local review guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md. Calibration: past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr01151.md, pr01224.md, pr02040.md, pr04037.md, pr04877.md; both cases and INDEX.md in not_misformalizations/.
review.notes: All three declarations were checked. Lean proofs in /workspace/review/scratch.lean establish that the ncard expression equals Mathlib's unlabelled, non-induced copyCount, that the counted set is finite, and that edge excess guarantees a positive count. The excess hypothesis is impossible for n < 4, including q = 0. A separate proved equivalence shows that the all-even-q and sufficiently-large-even-q unspecified-constant formulations agree after shrinking the constant; this is not another defect. Small C4 adjacency and labelled-copy enumerations were tested. The scratch proofs use no sorryAx. No answer(...) or formal_proof records occur in the file, and the reviewed file was not modified.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported discrepancy strengthens the cited result to additional even orders; it does not make the formal statement trivially true or demonstrably false. Every qualifying graph contains at least one C4, so any finite collection of small cases can be accommodated by decreasing the existential constant c. A disproof would require an unbounded family violating the square-root lower bound. Establishing the cited extremal-threshold gap itself requires substantial mathematics, not a short Lean computation.

submission.summary: No short, honest demonstration was found. The earlier finding concerns the scope of the cited theorem, not a known counterexample to the broader formalized claim. No trivial-proof file was created or retained, and no compilation is claimed.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported misformalization is an unsupported generalization of a genuine supersaturation result. Neither a trivial proof nor a trivial disproof follows from that discrepancy, and showing merely that an even integer need not be a power of two would not demonstrate a defect in the declaration's full hypothesis or conclusion.

submission.summary: Restricted q to even prime powers by requiring ∃ k : ℕ, q = 2 ^ (k + 1), while retaining the extremal-number threshold. Updated the docstring to identify the cited corollary and explain why finitely many small q can be included by decreasing the positive constant. No other declarations were changed. The requested compile command succeeded with only the permitted `sorry` warnings.
